Any folder whose name starts with `mock` or `__mock` is now classified as test code (mock resources), whatever the rest of the name is. The new test passes. I only ran that test class, not the rest of the module's tests.

In `TestConventions.java` (`codeanalyzer/src/main/java/nl/obren/sokrates/sourcecode/scoping/`), I changed the two mock-folder patterns:
- `.*/mock[a-zA-Z0-9_\- ]+/.*` became `.*/mock[^/\\]*/.*`.
- `.*/__mock[a-zA-Z0-9_\- ]+/.*` became `.*/__mock[^/\\]*/.*`.

The rest of the folder name can now be anything except a path separator. That covers a plain `mock/` folder, `mock.data`, `mock(old)`, `mock-größe` and `mock模拟`. The match stays within one folder name, and the rule already handled Windows-style paths with backslashes.

I added `TestConventionsTest.java` under `codeanalyzer/src/test/java/nl/obren/sokrates/sourcecode/scoping/`. It checks these cases, with both `/` and `\` separators:
- **Test code:** `mock`, `mocks`, `__mocks__`, `mock-data`, `mock_data`, `mock data`, `mockStore`, `mock.data`, `mock(old)`, `mock-größe`, `mock模拟`.
- **Not test code:** `remock/`, `demo/`, `src/main/java/`, `mock.java`, `mockery.java`.

I didn't commit anything.
